[Crash]: Crash while JEI registers vanilla Anvil category: invalid AIR drawable ingredient
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Crash

Environment from the latest log
- Minecraft: 1.20.1
- Forge: 47.4.10
- Java: 17.0.15, Microsoft
- JEI: 15.74.0.227
- Apotheosis: 7.4.8
- Placebo: 8.6.3
- AttributesLib: 1.3.7
- Jade: 11.13.2+forge
- Goety: 2.5.57.3
- OS: Windows 10 x64
- Launcher: Prism Launcher
Steps to reproduce
1. Launch the instance with the modpack with APOTHEOSIS included and JEI
2. Load the world / join the server.
3. Wait for JEI to register its recipe categories.
4. The client crashes during registration of the vanilla Anvil category, trying to opening the inventory

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

_No response_

### Extra Notes (Optional)

_No response_

### Crash Report

 The client crashes with: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Ingredient is invalid and cannot be used as a drawable ingredient: 0 air minecraft:air  at mezz.jei.library.gui.helpers.GuiHelper.lambda$createDrawableIngredient$0(GuiHelper.java:177) at mezz.jei.library.gui.helpers.GuiHelper.createDrawableIngredient(GuiHelper.java:175) at mezz.jei.api.helpers.IGuiHelper.createDrawableItemLike(IGuiHelper.java:195) at mezz.jei.library.plugins.vanilla.anvil.AnvilRecipeCategory.<init>(AnvilRecipeCategory.java:35) at mezz.jei.library.plugins.vanilla.VanillaPlugin.registerCategories(VanillaPlugin.java:219) at mezz.jei.library.load.PluginLoader.createRecipeCategories(PluginLoader.java:149) at mezz.jei.library.load.PluginLoader.createRecipeManager(PluginLoader.java:154) at mezz.jei.library.startup.JeiStarter.start(JeiStarter.java:115) The same AIR ingredient exception appears more than once during category registration. Isolation results - Removing JEI prevents the crash. - Reinstalling the official Apotheosis JAR does not prevent it. - The fatal stack trace points to JEI’s vanilla Anvil category, not Apotheosis’s SocketingRecipe. The attached latest.log and debug.log contain the full traces. The logs also include a separate Apotheosis/Jade tooltip ClassCastException involving Goety blocks; it appears distinct from this fatal Anvil-category exception. Version mismatch to verify before submitting: you previously listed Forge 47.4.23, but this latest log reports 47.4.10. Use the versions actually involved in the reproduction, or test once with the intended Forge version.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Add category extensions for vanilla cooking recipe categories such as smelting and blasting
issues.body:
### Suggestion

Currently, there is no way to add a category extension for a vanilla cooking category, only crafting, brewing, and smithing are supported. I have a few dynamic furnace recipes that would be nice to implement as a single recipe in JEI with focus links as opposed to my current solution of generating fake recipes into JEI.

One challenge with furnace categories is the fact there are 4 nearly identical furnace categories that vary in just type. It would be nice to be able to register just a single extension for all 4 categories (or at least the 3 with fuel) by specifying an interface they all implement (this would create a category of the form `T extends AbstractCookingRecipe & YourInterface`). However, that may not be practical with how the category extensions are setup, so it may be necessary to just create a base class and 4 subclasses then register those separately.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Add a way to set `getSourceRecipeIds ` without creating a recipe extension.
issues.body:
### Suggestion

The new `IRecipeCategory#getSourceRecipeIds` is nice for marking the source of generated recipes, but I was having trouble finding a good way to set it on vanilla recipes. For a mod added recipe, I can simply add a `sourceIds()` method to my recipe interface and query that in the recipe category, but I cannot change the JEI categories to override the method. This leaves my only choice to create an extension of the category for my custom instance which requires reimplementing the standard recipe logic just to display the source IDs.

Given JEI cannot modify the vanilla recipe classes to add this functionality, my proposal would be an interface you can implement on any vanilla recipe, which JEI will check for in the vanilla categories. This means all the mod has to do is extend the vanilla recipe object to add the interface rather than needing to add a category extension.

issues.title: Bookmark list fully hidden when FTB Library sidebar is in a left corner (regression in 29.47.0.109)
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

1. Minecraft 26.1.2, NeoForge 26.1.2.109, JEI 29.47.0.109, FTB Library 26.1.2.9.
2. Bookmark a few items in JEI.
3. Enable the FTB Library sidebar at TOP_LEFT or BOTTOM_LEFT (/ftblibrary clientconfig).
4. Open the player inventory or a crafting table.

### Expected Behavior

The bookmark list stays visible, skipping only the slots covered by the sidebar's exclusion area (this is how JEI 29.43.0.107 behaves).

### Actual Behavior

The whole bookmark list disappears in the inventory and crafting table. It reappears if the sidebar is disabled or moved to TOP_RIGHT/BOTTOM_RIGHT. Bookmarks still show on screens without the sidebar, e.g. the settings screen.

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

https://www.feed-the-beast.com/modpacks/135-ftb-evolution-2

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

1.3.0

### Extra Notes (Optional)

Regression from 29.43.0.107 -> 29.47.0.109; FTB Library jar is unchanged between the two.
FTB Library reports one small exclusion rectangle (size of its button grid, 17 px cells) in the chosen corner via getGuiExtraAreas.
Setting bookmarkList layoutMode = MAXIMIZE_AVAILABLE_SPACE does not help, nor does BOTTOM_LEFT or fewer sidebar buttons.
Possibly related 29.47 changelog entries: "Shrink ingredient and bookmark grids to fit their contents", "Hide empty ingredient grids while keeping search usable", "Route GUI input through input areas and captured interactions".
Workaround: put the sidebar on the right side.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Default IRecipeCategory#getSourceRecipeIds to filter out synthetic recipe ids rather than requiring it to be overridden
issues.body:
### Suggestion

Copied from a message I sent on discord:

https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/commit/92e30b8ac1c004f66b770d5b1020984aa65b810f#diff-a572546d8aa1b178374dfde26a9847723261e7671360de1b20da348cc2f19d7cR196 imo it would make sense to have the default filter out the more standardized synthetic ids. Afaik EMI set a precedent of synthetic recipes being: [`<namespace>:/<path>`](https://github.com/emilyploszaj/emi/blob/81f6453c0d0b6df2e503d0bc5f19f1c73fd12173/xplat/src/main/java/dev/emi/emi/api/recipe/EmiRecipe.java#L27-L29) (because normal resolved folders can't have the identifier start with / as there is no corresponding folder). So if getIdentifier returns a path that starts with / it is almost certainly a mod following the precedent that EMI started for what is a synthetic recipe id, and thus based on your docs for getSourceRecipeIds shouldn't be included.

That being said, it isn't a bad idea for synthetic recipe categories to override that method to optimize out querying the recipe id, but that is sort of more of a micro optimization

issues.title: [Other]: What change between versions 15.49.0.200 and 15.55.0.201 doubled my load times?
issues.body:
### Other

I want to note that I am not sure that this is a bug, exactly, though I am curious if there is a config that I can disable to change the behavior. I maintain a very, very large personal modpack, which, by way of including both Every Compat and Paladin's furniture, two mods which create large amounts of dynamic resources, tends to have extremely high JEI loading times. I fully understand that this is because of the size of my modpack and that multiple dynamic mods can create exponential amounts of items and increase load times. This is fine, and I understand that this is not a bug. However, versions of JEI after 15.49.0.200 have caused my load times to double. I know some config changes occurred between versions, however I changed every config I could find to align with their settings before updates - however this did not help. I want to make it very, very clear that I understand my modpack is absolutely crazy and having 20+ minute JEI load times is also crazy, however I've been working on this modpack for fun for years and I'm used to this. I'm not asking or seeking support for my absurd modpack, I am simply looking for info on which change or config from 15.49.0.200 to 15.55.0.201 might double load times (in this case from 20 minutes to 40, and yes I understand this is crazy) with high numbers of items.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Better Integration with Non-Modded Servers
issues.body: ### Suggestion JEI is a very popular mod and is included in almost every modpack. However, modern servers often have many custom ways of obtaining items that JEI currently cannot represent. For example: * Custom crafting recipes (workbenches) * NPC trades * Shops * Mob drops (e.g. MythicMobs) * More advanced/custom crafting systems (e.g. Custom Grid) ## Proposal I propose adding an API/overlay that would allow a server to send recipe information to the client through a custom packet. The server could provide information such as: * **Grid size / I/O layout** * For example, a standard 3×3 grid * Or even a fully custom layout, such as: ``` X X X X X Z Z X Z Z ``` Where `X` represents an available slot and `Z` represents an empty/non-interactive area. * **Recipe name** * For example: `Alchemy Table` * **Chance / probability** * Useful for recipes with random outputs or drops * **Custom model / entity** * For example, support for ModelEngine models or custom entities * **Resource pack-based GUI/grid** * Allow the server to provide or reference a custom visual representation of the crafting grid * **Description / additional information** * Custom text explaining how the recipe works * **Inputs and outputs** * Including multiple inputs, outputs, quantities, and potentially different result possibilities This would allow JEI to act as a bridge between modded and server-side content, without requiring the server to actually be modded. ### Example Use Case A server could send a packet describing a custom **Alchemy Table** recipe: ```text Name: Alchemy Table Grid: X X X X X Z Z X Z Z Input: - 2x Iron Ingot - 1x Diamond - 3x Redstone Output: - 1x Custom Alchemy Crystal Chance: - 75% Description: "Time: 40 sec" ``` JEI could then display this recipe alongside normal modded recipes, making custom server content discoverable in the same way. This could be especially useful for large servers that rely heavily on plugins such as **MythicMobs, ModelEngine, custom crafting systems, NPCs, shops, and custom resource packs**, while still keeping the client completely vanilla from the server's perspective. The goal would be to make JEI more useful on modern servers without requiring a dedicated client-side mod for every custom server system. An example of the appearance from a mod that could be sent by the non-modded server.

issues.title: [Bug]: JEI shows missing-texture checkerboard on Connected-Texture (CT) items
issues.body: ### Steps to Reproduce the Bug **Summary:** JEI's item list renders a magenta/black missing-texture checkerboard for several items, bleeding into the tooltip of the adjacent hovered item. The same items render correctly in-world and in their own mod's JEI category page — this only happens in JEI's general item list. ## Environment - Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.250 - JEI 19.57.0.447 (`jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.57.0.447.jar`) - Create 6.0.10 (`create-1.21.1-6.0.10.jar`) - Create Deco 2.1.3 (`createdeco-2.1.3.jar`) - Design n' Decor 2.2b (`Design-n-Decor-1.21.1-2.2b.jar`) - Create: Bits 'n' Bobs 2.3.5 (`bits_n_bobs-2.3.5.jar`) ## Affected items All items identified so far come from mods that register blocks through Create's Connected Texture (CT) sprite-shifting API (`com.simibubi.create.foundation.block.connected.CTSpriteShifter`): - Create Deco — shipping container/vault blocks - Design n' Decor — vault/container blocks, sheet metal, girders, deepslate tiles, stone metal, dark metal - Create: Bits 'n' Bobs — grating panels, weathered girders ## Likely cause CT blocks choose their sprite based on neighboring blocks in the world at render time. JEI's item-list icon rendering has no such neighbor context, which is consistent with these blocks rendering correctly in-world and broken only in JEI's isolated icon rendering. ## Similar reports - https://github.com/AllTheMods/All-the-Mons/issues/655 — connected-texture (Rechiseled) blocks showing missing texture specifically in JEI, fine in-world. - https://github.com/terrarium-earth/Chipped/issues/215 — same "missing texture in JEI GUI" symptom. ### Expected Behavior JEI's item list should render these CT blocks using their default/unconnected sprite (the same icon shown in their own mod's JEI category page and creative tab), not a missing-texture checkerboard. ### Actual Behavior JEI's item list renders a magenta/black missing-texture checkerboard for several items, bleeding into the tooltip of the adjacent hovered item. The same items render correctly in-world and in their own mod's JEI category page — this only happens in JEI's general item list. ### Mod Pack URL (Optional) _No response_ ### Mod Pack Version (Optional) _No response_ ### Extra Notes (Optional) _No response_ ### latest.log https://gist.github.com/Telmarine/bfd032ad796e236a588a4c016f4ffe69

issues.title: [Crash]: Create 6.0.10 Causes JEI 19.56.0.441 Crash
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Crash

Based on the log file you provided, the problem with JEI is a hard code conflict with the Create mod (create-1.21.1-6.0.10.jar).

The critical crash error preventing JEI from indexing ingredients on world join is:

`java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: An interpreter is already registered for this: create:potion`

Why this is happening:

Both Create and another active mod are trying to register a sub-type interpreter for fluid potions (`create:potion`) inside the JEI registry map simultaneously. Java does not allow double-registrations on the same hook, forcing JEI to throw an `IllegalArgumentException` and lock up.

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

_No response_

### Extra Notes (Optional)

Codename Ancient Builder X3 preparing a modpack for a server host owner expecting 50+ players to play this

### Crash Report

https://gist.github.com/Bopkasen/3d5a2e8de1fe59048ff37fb3fa1e43bb

How to Fix It

Fix 1: Step down your primary JEI version (Recommended)You are currently running jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.56.0.441.jar. The 19.56.x branch altered how custom fluid registries are handled.

Close your game entirely.

Navigate to your ATLauncher instance folder: 📂 config/almostunified/unification/.Open the mods/ directory and delete jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.56.0.441.jar.

Download and install Just Enough Items (JEI) version 19.21.0.166 (or any build in the stable 19.21.x milestone branch for 1.21.1). 

This step-down will safely parse the duplicate fluid tags without crashing the engine.

Fix 2: Add Create Potions to your Almost Unified Exclusions

Since the fluid collision is overlapping with your unification data maps, you can use your common.json file that you configured earlier to make the unification engine completely ignore the potion conflict:

Open 📂 config/almostunified/common.json.Locate the "ignored_items": [] array block.

Register the create potion item reference inside the brackets: "ignored_items": ["create:potion"].

issues.title: [Bug]: Bookmark transfer on Shift + left click does nothing — the quick-move bind consumes the click
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

Transferring a bookmarked recipe uses `key.jei.transferRecipeBookmark`, which is handled in
`RecipeBookmarkElement#handleClick`. Its default gesture is Shift + left click on a bookmark.

To reproduce, you need a container whose recipe transfer is registered by a mod through
`IUniversalRecipeTransferHandler` — I used a Create: Redstone Requester, which has 9 ghost slots.
Bookmark a recipe that can be transferred into that container, hover the bookmark in the overlay,
then hold Shift and left click it.

### Expected Behavior

The bookmarked recipe is transferred into the container, the same way it is on a vanilla container
with JEI's built-in transfer handler.

### Actual Behavior

Nothing happens. The handler only ever runs its simulate pass — the `doTransfer == true` branch is
never reached — and the click is reported as unhandled, so it falls through to the next input layer.

### Root Cause

Two different JEI actions are bound to the same default gesture, Shift + left click:

- `key.jei.transferRecipeBookmark` — the bookmark transfer above (default Shift + left click).
- `key.jei.quickMove` (`IInternalKeyMappings#getQuickMove`) — quick-moving an item into/out of a
  ghost slot (default Shift + left click).

With Shift held, the quick-move path consumes the click before the bookmark handler gets to run its
real pass, so `transferRecipe(..., doTransfer = true)` is never called. That is why the handler's
simulate path is the only thing that shows up.

This is independent of the container implementation, but is most visible on containers that are not
vanilla-shaped (e.g. Create: Redstone Requester), since those are the ones that go through a custom
transfer handler at all.

### Extra Notes

Tested on 19.56.0.438 for 1.21.1 with NeoForge 21.1.248.

Additional env: [Create 6.0.10](https://modrinth.com/mod/create/version/6.0.10+mc1.21.1), [Create: Cyber Goggles 8.6.3](https://modrinth.com/mod/create-cyber-goggles/version/1.21.1-8.6.3-NeoForge)

The code in question: [`mezz/jei/gui/overlay/elements/RecipeBookmarkElement.java`](https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/blob/1.21.1/Gui/src/main/java/mezz/jei/gui/overlay/elements/RecipeBookmarkElement.java)

issues.title: [Bug]: If a focus matches multiple inputs, they are "randomly" shuffled.
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

JEI collects focused ingredients as indices in a set, notably using an [IntOpenHashSet](https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/blob/1.20.1/Library/src/main/java/mezz/jei/library/ingredients/DisplayIngredientAcceptor.java#L209) which does not guarantee iteration order. The result is the ingredient order on focus is "randomly" swapped based on hash set iteration order.

To reproduce, you will need a recipe that has multiple NBT variants of an item on output that return the same subtype. Alternatively, if you have an ingredient subtype interpreter that distinguishes them but a recipe subtype interpreter that does not and you look up recipes for a NBT variant not shown. Alternatively, use multiple focuses, however that is achieved.

### Expected Behavior

Focused ingredients would filter the list without changing the order.

### Actual Behavior

Focusing changes the order of ingredients if multiple match.

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

_No response_

### Extra Notes (Optional)

Tested on JEI 15.59.0.210 for 1.20.1.

This issue is mostly cosmetic so far as it seems when focus links are involved, the linked slot will be reordered to match the shuffled set.

The fix for this issue is relatively straight forward, it seems [this loop](https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/blob/1.20.1/Library/src/main/java/mezz/jei/library/gui/recipes/layout/builder/RecipeSlotBuilder.java#L269-L276) is in charge of iteration over the focused set. It could be swapped to iteration over the ingredient indices with a filter instead. Alternatively, switching to a set that guarantees iteration order or sorting the indices before iteration would help.

Example fixed code:
```java
for (int i = 0; i < allIngredients.size(); i++) {
  if (focusMatches.contains(i)) {
    focusedIngredients.add(allIngredients.get(i));
  }
}
```

### Other

Hi mezz,

I’m the maintainer of JEIU, an unofficial fork of JEI: [JEIU](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/jei-unofficial). It adds features aimed at large modpacks and incorporates some code from GTNH NEI and other projects. It is released under the applicable open-source licenses, with the corresponding credits and license notices preserved.

I’d like to apologize for not reaching out earlier to introduce the project. I understand that complying with an open-source license does not require prior permission, but given how closely this project is connected to JEI, giving you a heads-up would have been more considerate.

I also noticed that a user reported a JEIU issue to your repository: https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/issues/4481. I’m sorry for the additional work this has caused you in identifying and handling the report.

I’ve explained the relationship between JEIU and the official JEI on CurseForge, MC百科 (mcmod.cn), and other project pages, and asked users to report JEIU-specific issues to our issue tracker. I’ll also follow up on misdirected reports that come to my attention, direct users to our repository, and continue improving these notices to help reduce the burden on you.

If you have any concerns about the project’s name, how its relationship with the official JEI is presented, or the maintenance burden it creates for you, please let me know. I’ll take them seriously and work to address them.

Thank you for your continued work on JEI. This project would not exist without it.

Besides,please feel free to close this issue.

StardustMINUS.

issues.title: [Bug]: JEI does not refresh recipes when switching between servers with different custom recipes through Velocity
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

1. Set up a Velocity proxy with at least two backend servers.
2. Configure both backend servers with server-side custom recipes.
3. Make sure the recipe sets are different between the backend servers.
4. Install the corresponding JEI client mod.
5. Connect to backend server A through Velocity.
6. Open JEI and verify that the recipes from server A are displayed correctly.
7. Switch to backend server B through Velocity without restarting the Minecraft client.
8. Open JEI and inspect an item whose recipe differs between server A and server B.

### Expected Behavior

After switching backend servers, JEI should discard the recipe state from the previous server and refresh its internal recipe data using the recipes synchronized by the newly connected server.

### Actual Behavior

After switching backend servers, JEI may keep using the recipe state from the previous server.

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

_No response_

### Extra Notes (Optional)

I tried a fix for this issue on Minecraft 26.2, and it worked in my test environment.

The fix includes:

- injecting after `ClientPacketListener#handleUpdateRecipes`;
- reading the final synchronized recipe container from the client connection;
- converting the synchronized recipes into a JEI `RecipeMap`;
- passing the updated recipe map through the JEI lifecycle event;
- replacing JEI's stored server-synchronized recipe state;
- stopping and restarting the JEI runtime when the recipe set changes;
- removing the previous Fabric recipe synchronization listener to avoid keeping stale recipe data;
- adding a regression test that switches the client between backend servers with different recipe sets.

With this change, JEI correctly refreshes its recipes after switching between Velocity backend servers in my Minecraft 26.2 test setup.

issues.title: [Bug]: New non-default method added to `ITypedIngredient` on 1.20, causing a potential `NoSuchMethodError`
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

In JEI 15.35.0.175, a new non-default method `ITypedIngredient#cast` was added. This leads to an unimplemented method for any mods who implemented that interface previously.

While normally that would be fine as the interface is marked `@NonExtendable`, it was not NonExtendable until 15.14.0 which was well after the start of 1.20, and the methods to create clickable ingredients did not exist until 15.19.2 (also well after the start of 1.20). As a result, mods such as Tinkers' Construct have an implementation of `ITypedIngredient` that predates those APIs.

I am not sure this actually causes any crashes; I am not able to get one from a quick test. But it seems worth elevating to a separate issue as it might cause an issue in the future with newer JEI and older Tinkers. I plan to migrate to the factory methods but #4453 is currently blocking that.

### Expected Behavior

New methods added to interfaces that were previously not `@NonExtendable` would be `default`.

### Actual Behavior

New method was added that required implementing on an interface that existed previously.

issues.title: [Bug]: Generic Mismatch between `IGuiContainerHandler` and `IClickableIngredientFactory`
issues.body: ### Steps to Reproduce the Bug To implement `IGuiContainerHandler`, you need to provide a `Optional>`. The JEI docs currently recommend implementing it using `IClickableIngredientFactory` to create instances of `IClickableIngredient`, however, the builder methods there provide an output of `Optional>` (e.g. `Optional>`), and Java does not allow returning `T` as `?` via the nested generics. It seems `IIngredientManager#createClickableIngredient` has the same issue. With my previous approach that did not use `IClickableIngredientFactory`, I had no trouble returning `Optional.of(new ClickableIngredient<>(...))`, which suggests to me the only issue is the return type of the `IBuilder#buildWithArea`. A suggested solution would be providing a second version of each method that returns `Optional>` (which can run basically the same code). Alternatively, the builder could just return a `IClickableIngredient` as I cannot see the usecase for it returning an empty optional; you need the value to create the builder. ### Expected Behavior To not see a generic error that requires an unchecked cast when using the JEI API. ### Actual Behavior I get this error when using the recommended APIs: ### Mod Pack URL (Optional) _No response_ ### Mod Pack Version (Optional) _No response_ ### Extra Notes (Optional) Just updated to using JEI 15.49.0.194 for 1.20.1 when I encountered this error. I can work around this issue with casts, but due to the location I am required to do some very ugly casts or a wasteful map: ```java return (Optional>)(Optional) factory.createBuilder(ForgeTypes.FLUID_STACK, fluid.fluid()).buildWithArea(fluid.location()); return factory.createBuilder(ForgeTypes.FLUID_STACK, fluid.fluid()).buildWithArea(fluid.location()).map(Function.identity()); ``` I will note before trying to migrate to this API, I did have my own implementation of `ITypedIngredient`/`IClickableIngredient`, which now errored as `#cast` did not previous exist. This might cause issues when players use the newer version of JEI on older versions. Since the `@ApiStatus.NonExtendable` was not previously on the API, I think it would be prudent to make the new `cast` method default; the implementation from `TypedIngredient` is generic enough to copy to the interface. I went ahead and reported this as #4454. ### latest.log _No response_

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Allow tagging creative tabs as `c:hidden_from_recipe_viewers` to skip adding their items to JEI.
issues.body:
### Suggestion

## Problem

I have some creative tabs that are filled with useful items for creative mode players, but are often considered clutter by modpack makers. This largely consists of cosmetic variants of our blocks, such as wood variants of crafting tables and alike, which are a little annoying to have to filter down with search. It would be useful to have a method to skip these items being added to creative.

I have in the past used `removeIngredientsAtRuntime`, but this can be slow on low memory search with large numbers of items (#3882). Additionally, it and adds the ingredients to a global blacklist which can break some recipes and catalysts (see also #4238), for instance it hides all hidden variants from the output of the recipe breaking the focus link between slots.

## Suggested Solution

Since around 1.19.3, creative tabs are now a registry, which means they support tags. JEI could ignore any creative tabs tagged as `c:hidden_from_recipe_viewers` from populating the item list. I can then relocate any such items to a single creative tab, and tag it to ensure it is skipped JEI without worrying about the downsides of `removeIngredientsAtRuntime`. Modpack makers if they wish to show those variants can simply remove the tag.

From a previous discussion on discord, this should be the spot to patch with the tag check: https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/blob/71ec02e965d82897adcaa28cf2f277056f1d36a8/Library/src/main/java/mezz/jei/library/plugins/vanilla/ingredients/ItemStackListFactory.java#L71

The tag's application on creative tabs will also need to be documented somewhere that is easy for both mod devs and pack devs to locate.

## Other considerations

It might be useful to also have a method to blacklist a creative tab at runtime apart from the tag. For tinkers case, we also have a config option that limits the shown tool variants in creative. If I were able to blacklist a tab at runtime, I could then just add the specific tools I wish to be visible using `addIngredientsAtRuntime`.

Doing this via the tag requires me to always blacklist the tab, which would mean I just have to always add the ingredients at runtime. This is not a huge problem for me as I have the code to handle that already, but it may be more efficient to not have to cancel the tab addition and use the runtime feature.

So ultimately this is up to you whether you want a second API in addition to the tag that does this.

issues.title: [Crash]: Severe freeze (~13s) during "Registering item subtypes" causes disconnection when joining a world, due to JEI integration
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Crash

When connecting to a modded world (Forge 1.20.1) with both JEI and Lightman's Currency installed, the client freezes for approximately 13 seconds during the "Registering item subtypes" step, executed on the main render thread. This freeze is severe enough that it causes the client to become unresponsive to server packets, resulting in a disconnection/timeout shortly after joining. Disabling JEI entirely resolves the issue completely; the freeze/disconnect does not occur without JEI.

Environment:
Minecraft: 1.20.1
Forge: 47.4.10
JEI: latest available version for 1.20.1 (tested, issue persists)
Lightman's Currency: latest available version for 1.20.1 (2.3.0.4e, tested, issue persists)
Modpack: 159 mods, ~108 mod files (custom pack, includes Create, MineColonies, AE2, Farmer's Delight, and many others)
Connection method: Essential Mod's Session Play Server (SPS) / hosting feature (P2P via Essential relay)

Steps to reproduce:

Host a world with the modpack described above (JEI + Lightman's Currency both enabled) using Essential's world hosting feature.
Have a second player join via Essential invite.
Observe the client log during connection: item subtype registration for lightmanscurrency:lightmanscurrency takes ~13 seconds.
During this freeze, the client stops responding (world appears frozen, entities don't move, GUIs fail to load).
Shortly after, the client disconnects from the server (likely a timeout, as the client isn't processing keep-alive packets during the freeze).

Relevant log excerpt:

[17:58:10] [pool-42-thread-1/ERROR]: Registering item subtypes: lightmanscurrency:lightmanscurrency is running and has taken 5.094 seconds so far
[17:58:15] [pool-42-thread-1/ERROR]: Registering item subtypes: lightmanscurrency:lightmanscurrency is running and has taken 10.09 seconds so far
[17:58:18] [Render thread/INFO]: Registering item subtypes: lightmanscurrency:lightmanscurrency took 13.12 seconds

Additional notes:

This freeze happens on every single connection attempt (tested across multiple reconnects in the same session), not just the first time.
We suspect the cause is the large number of item subtype variants Lightman's Currency registers (coins, coin piles, coin blocks across 6 coin types, wallets, tickets, etc.), which JEI's subtype interpreter has to process synchronously on the main thread.
We already tried: updating both JEI and Lightman's Currency to their latest 1.20.1 releases — issue persists identically.
Workaround currently in use: disabling JEI entirely. This fully resolves the freeze and disconnection, confirming JEI's integration with Lightman's Currency as the root cause.

Suggested fix direction:
Moving the subtype interpreter registration (or at least the expensive part of it) off the main/render thread, or caching/precomputing it asynchronously before the player fully joins, would likely resolve the freeze without requiring JEI to be disabled.

Happy to provide the full client log or a debug log if useful for reproducing/diagnosing this further.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Make a recipe slot's rendering, displayed ingredient, hover test and ingredient set pluggable
issues.body:
### Suggestion

## What we do

LDLib2 is a UI library. We want to renders our own elements behave like real JEI 
slots — tooltips, click-to-lookup, bookmarks, focus, transfer.

We don't mixin JEI, but we do compile against the implementation jar and call non-API
classes to make that work.

Especially with the recent frequent updates, and with NeoForge updates driving more of
them, I have had to do a lot of work to keep our JEI compatibility alive. This is not
really a problem with JEI — we are the ones using non-API classes. But I don't think it is
a good situation either, and I expect that with AI-assisted development, JEI will see more
frequent internal restructuring in the near future. So I would rather ask for support at
the **API level**.

## What we need

A JEI slot is currently one indivisible bundle: geometry, rendering, the displayed
ingredient, the ingredient set, and the tooltip. **We need each of those five to be
pluggable**, because our UI already owns them.

### 1. Custom rendering — JEI should not draw the slot

Our elements draw themselves: custom textures, animated progress overlays, fluid bars, 3D
block scenes, arbitrary sizes, all under a `PoseStack` transform. We need a slot that
carries semantics only and renders nothing.

Today we fake it: an empty `ISlottedRecipeWidget` registered via
`addSlottedWidget(widget, List.of(slot))` suppresses the drawing, and size comes from a
dummy `IIngredientRenderer` whose `render()` is empty and whose `getWidth()/getHeight()`
return our size. Both are tricks that happen to work, not contracts.

> `IRecipeSlotBuilder#setNoRenderer()`, or `IRecipeExtrasBuilder#addExternallyDrawnSlot(...)`
> — an explicit "the plugin draws this one" mode.

### 2. Custom displayed ingredient, evaluated dynamically

**This is the one that matters most,** because the displayed ingredient is what JEI's
lookup, bookmark, focus/highlight and tooltip all target. If JEI picks it while we render
something else, the player hovers item A and looks up item B — that's a bug, not a
cosmetic mismatch.

Our slots don't cycle on JEI's schedule and we don't what to use it. Contents come from customizable data and can change every dynamicly;

### 3. Custom hover test — the predicate, not the size

We need to answer "is the mouse over this slot" ourselves. Not "a different fixed
rectangle": our elements sit under a transform, can be clipped by a scroll container, can
be non-rectangular, and can move or resize every frame.

Today `RecipeSlot` holds an `ImmutableRect2i` and only exposes `setPosition(int, int)`, so
we implement `IRecipeSlotDrawable` purely to override `isMouseOver` — after which
`getRect()` / `getAreaIncludingBackground()` have to throw, because we can't answer them
honestly, our ui support any shape(not only rect) and transform.

### 4. Custom "all possible ingredients", evaluated dynamically

A slot's full alternatives set — every item in a tag, every fluid a machine accepts — is
what external consumers read: the tag tooltip, other plugins walking `IRecipeSlotView`,
our own lookup helpers. Ours is computed from live data.

We understand the recipe **search index** is built once in `setRecipe` and can't reasonably
be dynamic; that part is fine as it is. What we need dynamic is the runtime
`IRecipeSlotView#getAllIngredientsList()`. Today `RecipeSlot.allIngredients` is `final`,
fixed at construction, so we pass a `Supplier<List<ITypedIngredient<?>>>` through our own
implementation instead.

### 5. JEI's tooltip for whatever we're currently displaying, plus our own lines

Given the ingredient **we** decided to display, we need JEI's tooltip for it — mod name,
tag name, tag contents, respecting the user's JEI config — and the ability to append our
own lines to it.

`IRecipeSlotRichTooltipCallback` covers appending, but only for a slot JEI owns and only
when JEI decides that slot is hovered. When our UI is hovered outside a JEI slot, or when
we need to render the tooltip ourselves, there's nothing: `ITooltipBuilder` exists, but
nothing populates it from an `ITypedIngredient` and nothing renders it. So we hand-copied
`RecipeSlot`'s *private* `getTooltip` / `addTagNameTooltip` / `addIngredientsToTooltip`.

## How we do it today

Two places, and between them three mechanisms used for something other than their intent.

**In `setRecipe`** we declare real JEI slots, because that is what gets indexed for recipe
search and lookup. But they must be invisible, and their size must match our element. The
ingredient renderer is the only lever for either:

```java
var slotBuilder = builder.addSlot(role)
        .addTypedIngredients(ingredients)
        .setSlotName(SLOT_PREFIX + index)
        .setPosition(area.getX(), area.getY());

for (ITypedIngredient<?> ingredient : ingredients) {
    var type = ingredient.getType();
    slotBuilder.setCustomRenderer(type, new IIngredientRenderer() {
        @Override
        public void render(GuiGraphics guiGraphics, Object ingredient) {}   // we already drew it

        @Override
        public List<Component> getTooltip(Object ingredient, TooltipFlag tooltipFlag) {
            return List.of();
        }

        @Override
        public int getWidth() { return area.getWidth(); }                   // the only setSize we have

        @Override
        public int getHeight() { return area.getHeight(); }
    });
}
```

An empty `render()` is our "don't draw this slot", and `getWidth()/getHeight()` is our
missing `IRecipeSlotBuilder#setSize`. We install it once per ingredient type in the slot,
because `setCustomRenderer` is keyed by `IIngredientType`.

**In `createRecipeExtras`** we then use `addSlottedWidget` twice, in opposite directions.

To give a slot a hit test of our own, we register a slotted widget that owns **no** slots
and produces one on demand from our own predicate:

```java
builder.addSlottedWidget(new ISlottedRecipeWidget() {
    @Override
    public Optional<RecipeSlotUnderMouse> getSlotUnderMouse(double mouseX, double mouseY) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(ourSlot.getRecipeSlots(mouseX, mouseY));  // our own hit test
    }

    @Override
    public ScreenPosition getPosition() {
        return ModularUIJEIWidget.ZERO;   // our coordinates are already absolute
    }
}, List.of());                            // <-- deliberately empty
```

JEI never learns the slot exists until we hand it over at hover time, which is how we get
around the fixed `ImmutableRect2i` in (3). The slot we return is our own
`IRecipeSlotDrawable`, so this is also the point where (2), (4) and (5) enter — everything
downstream of it (tooltip, lookup, bookmark, highlight) targets whatever that object says.

And to suppress the slots we declared back in `setRecipe`, we register the exact opposite:
a widget that **owns** the slot but never reports it as hovered.

```java
builder.getRecipeSlots().findSlotByName(SLOT_PREFIX + index).ifPresent(found ->
    builder.addSlottedWidget(new ISlottedRecipeWidget() {
        @Override
        public Optional<RecipeSlotUnderMouse> getSlotUnderMouse(double mouseX, double mouseY) {
            return Optional.empty();      // never hoverable
        }

        @Override
        public ScreenPosition getPosition() {
            return ModularUIJEIWidget.ZERO;
        }
    }, List.of(found)));                  // <-- owning it is what stops JEI drawing it
```

So: an empty renderer to mean "invisible", a renderer's dimensions to mean "size", an empty
slot list to mean "I'll do the hit testing", and a non-empty slot list to mean "hide this".
None of it is wrong, and all of it works — but none of it is what these APIs are for, which
is why we can't tell which parts will survive the next release.

## What that costs us today

To be clear: we **do** have all five working today, by implementing `IRecipeSlotDrawable`
ourselves. Functionally it works well — I thought it was a good solution. The cost is
maintenance, and it comes in two forms.

**`IRecipeSlotDrawable` is declared API, but it is not stable for implementors.**
Implementing it means implementing 17 abstract methods across it and `IRecipeSlotView` —
including ones we cannot answer honestly (`getRect()`, `getAreaIncludingBackground()`, see
(3) above) and three that are deprecated but still abstract, so they are dead code we're
required to write. Worse, its shape changes within a major version changed its apis — a hard compile break for anyone
implementing the interface. It reads like an interface meant to be *consumed*, not
*implemented*; but implementing it is currently the only way to get (1)–(5).

issues.title: [Bug]: IME preedit text is not rendered in the JEI search field
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

1. Enable an IME that uses composition text, such as Korean, Japanese, or Chinese.
2. Open an inventory with the JEI ingredient list visible.
3. Focus the JEI ingredient search field.
4. Start composing text without committing it.

This can also be reproduced in the creative inventory while the creative search tab is selected.

### Expected Behavior

The IME preedit text should be rendered at the cursor in the JEI ingredient search field.

In the creative inventory, the preedit overlay should remain in the JEI search field when that field has focus.

### Actual Behavior

The JEI search field does not receive the screen's preedit events, so composition text is not rendered there.

In the creative inventory, Minecraft forwards preedit events directly to its own search box, causing the preedit overlay to appear in the creative inventory search field instead of the focused JEI search field.

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

_No response_

### Extra Notes (Optional)

`GuiTextFieldFilter` extends Minecraft's `EditBox`, but it is rendered and managed outside the normal `Screen` listener hierarchy.

Additionally, `CreativeModeInventoryScreen#preeditUpdated` bypasses the currently focused screen listener and forwards the event directly to its own search box.

This affects both Fabric and NeoForge.

issues.title: Feature Request & Bug: Improve color search accuracy (add custom config) and fix Hotbar hotkeys (1-9) in multiplayer/Hypixel
issues.body:
### Suggestion

Hello! I often use JEI to build on multiplayer servers like Hypixel (specifically Build Battle), where I need to search for blocks by color and grab them as fast as possible. However, two major issues are currently slowing down my workflow.

1. Color Search Inaccuracies (Feature Request)
The color search algorithm (^) relies on pixel scanning, which creates massive inaccuracies due to shading and texture noise. For example:
- Green Concrete is classified as Brown
- Prismarine, Crimson Nylium, and several Shulker Boxes are tied to completely wrong colors.

Suggested Solutions for Colors:
- Supplement or replace the automatic pixel scan with official Minecraft block tags.
- (Alternative): Create a customizable configuration file (like `block_colors.txt` or `.json`) in the config folder, allowing users to manually map or override any block's color keywords.

2. Hotbar Number Hotkeys (1-9) Not Working on Servers (Bug Report)
When trying to grab items quickly, I cannot pull them into my hotbar instantly. Even when changing the giveMode to "INVENTORY" in the configuration file, it doesn't work on Hypixel. 

I understand that the standard click uses the /give command (which players don't have permission for on servers), but the feature where you hover over an item in the JEI overlay and press a number key (1, 2, 3, etc.) to send it to that hotbar slot is completely broken. 

I did a test using Roughly Enough Items (REI), and in REI, this exact feature (hovering and pressing 1-9) works perfectly fine even on Hypixel, without needing OP or commands. It would be amazing if JEI could handle hotbar slot injections the same way REI does, so we can use these hotkeys on multiplayer servers.

Thank you for your hard work on this mod!

issues.title: [Crash]: JEI triggers intermittent NPE in NeoForge's GenericPacketSplitter during world join ("Connection Lost — Invalid player data
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Crash

Environment

  • NeoForge: 21.1.242
  • Minecraft: 1.21.1
  • JEI version: 19.27.0.336 (jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.27.0.336.jar)
  • Loader: FML 4.0.43
  • Launcher: CurseForge App
  • OS: Windows 10 (amd64)
  • Java: 25.0.3 (Eclipse Adoptium)
  • Heap: 12.4 GB allocated
  • Mod count: ~150 mods (large modpack — Create ecosystem, Mekanism, Stellaris, Distant Horizons, FTB Chunks, KubeJS, etc. — full list below)

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Launch a heavily modded 1.21.1 NeoForge instance with JEI enabled alongside ~150 other mods.
  2. Join or create a singleplayer world.
  3. Intermittently, the client disconnects immediately after the login/config-sync phase with "Connection Lost / Invalid player data."
  4. Disabling JEI and repeating the launch multiple times in a row no longer reproduces the crash.

Stack Trace

[Render thread/ERROR] [net.minecraft.util.thread.BlockableEventLoop/FATAL]: Error executing task on Client
java.util.concurrent.CompletionException: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "io.netty.channel.ChannelHandlerContext.pipeline()" because the return value of "net.neoforged.neoforge.network.handling.IPayloadContext.channelHandlerContext()" is null
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.wrapInCompletionException(Unknown Source) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.encodeThrowable(Unknown Source) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.completeThrowable(Unknown Source) [?:?]
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture$AsyncSupply.run(Unknown Source) [?:?]

	at TRANSFORMER/minecraft@1.21.1/net.minecraft.util.thread.BlockableEventLoop.runAllTasks(BlockableEventLoop.java:111) [client-1.21.1-20240808.144430-srg.jar%23347!/:?]
	at TRANSFORMER/minecraft@1.21.1/net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.runTick(Minecraft.java:1155) [client-1.21.1-20240808.144430-srg.jar%23347!/:?]

	at TRANSFORMER/minecraft@1.21.1/net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(Main.java:230) [client-1.21.1-20240808.144430-srg.jar%23347!/:?]
	...
Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "io.netty.channel.ChannelHandlerContext.pipeline()" because the return value of "net.neoforged.neoforge.network.handling.IPayloadContext.channelHandlerContext()" is null
	at TRANSFORMER/neoforge@21.1.242/net.neoforged.neoforge.network.filters.GenericPacketSplitter.handle(GenericPacketSplitter.java:68) ~[neoforge-21.1.242-universal.jar%23348!/:?]
	at TRANSFORMER/neoforge@21.1.242/net.neoforged.neoforge.network.handling.MainThreadPayloadHandler.lambda$handle$0(MainThreadPayloadHandler.java:16) ~[neoforge-21.1.242-universal.jar%23348!/:?]
	at TRANSFORMER/minecraft@1.21.1/net.minecraft.util.thread.BlockableEventLoop.lambda$submitAsync$0(BlockableEventLoop.java:60) ~[client-1.21.1-20240808.144430-srg.jar%23347!/:?]
	... 23 more

[Render thread/ERROR] [net.neoforged.neoforge.network.registration.NetworkRegistry/]: Failed to process a synchronized task of the payload: neoforge:split

Note: The stack trace itself does not name any JEI class directly — the exception originates entirely inside NeoForge's own networking internals (GenericPacketSplitter/MainThreadPayloadHandler). This report is filed against JEI because repeated testing isolated JEI's presence as the reliable trigger, not because JEI code appears in the trace. It's possible JEI is sending a payload of a size/timing that reliably exposes an underlying NeoForge race condition, rather than JEI itself containing a bug — see "Additional Context" below.

Testing Performed

  • With JEI enabled: crash recurred intermittently across multiple launches of the same world.
  • With JEI disabled: multiple consecutive launches (5+) completed successfully with no crash, no disconnect, and normal world-join behavior.
  • Prior to isolating JEI, the following were also tested and ruled out as the primary cause (crash still recurred after each): removing Jade, removing DistantHorizons, reducing DistantHorizons' login-sync footprint (smaller sync radius, lower rate limit, lower bandwidth cap), enabling ModernFix's mixin.bugfix.packet_leak, and confirming JVM heap (12.4 GB allocated) was not a limiting factor.
  • Enabling NeoForge network DEBUG logging produced no additional diagnostic output leading up to the crash.
  • A Spark profiler hook (ModernFix's spark_profile_world_join) failed to capture data because the crash occurs before the world-join-complete event that triggers it.

Additional Context

  • This same GenericPacketSplitter NPE (and related encode-side EncoderException failures in the same class) has been reported against numerous unrelated mods and NeoForge builds from 21.1.23 through 21.1.242 over roughly two years, suggesting it may be a persistent, timing-dependent condition in NeoForge's GenericPacketSplitter/MainThreadPayloadHandler that different mods' payloads can trigger depending on size/timing, rather than a defect unique to any one mod's code.
  • If this turns out to be a NeoForge-side race condition rather than a JEI-specific bug, apologies in advance for filing here — happy to move this report to the NeoForge tracker if maintainers determine that's more appropriate. Flagging it with JEI first since testing consistently isolated JEI's presence/absence as the reproducible variable.

Expected Behavior

Joining a world with JEI installed should not intermittently disconnect the client due to a null channel handler context during payload splitting.

issues.title: [Suggestion]:  [Feature Request] Add config option to filter JEI display based on player's current inventory (like Vanilla Recipe Book)
issues.body:
### Suggestion

Currently JEI displays all items and recipes from all mods, but in survival mode players often want to see only what they can craft with the materials they already have in their inventory, similar to the vanilla recipe book.

I'd like to request a config option, e.g. showOnlyCraftable, which when enabled would filter JEI's item list to only show items that are craftable using the current player's inventory (including hotbar). Items that cannot be crafted should be hidden.

This option should be off by default to keep the current behavior, but when turned on it would greatly reduce visual clutter in large modpacks and make JEI more suited for exploration-based survival play.

Thanks for considering!

issues.title: [Bug]: Bookmark drag can get stuck after opening the recipe GUI from a bookmark
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

1. Launch the game with JEI installed.
2. Open an inventory/container screen where JEI's bookmark overlay is visible.
3. Add a recipe bookmark, for example a vanilla crafting recipe bookmark.
4. Re-enter the game or restart the client so the bookmark is loaded from JEI's bookmark config.
5. Open the inventory/container screen.
6. Click the recipe bookmark in the bookmark overlay for the first time.
7. Move the mouse.

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a recipe bookmark should open the recipe GUI or focus the recipe. If a bookmark drag was tentatively started on mouse down, it should always be canceled or completed when the GUI changes or when the mouse button is released.

### Actual Behavior

The bookmark's displayed ingredient icon may follow the mouse cursor, behaving like a stuck bookmark drag.

Subsequent clicks generally behave normally.

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

_No response_

### Extra Notes (Optional)

## Summary

When clicking a recipe bookmark in the bookmark overlay for the first time after entering the game, the bookmarked ingredient icon can remain attached to the mouse cursor, as if it is still being dragged.

This is reproducible with vanilla crafting recipe bookmarks, so it does not appear to be caused by a modded recipe category.

## Environment

- Minecraft: 26.1.2
- NeoForge: 26.1.2.0-beta
- JEI: 29.5.0.28
- Also checked source for JEI `v29.6.2`, `26.1`, and `26.2` branches; the relevant drag cleanup code appears unchanged.

## Analysis

The issue appears to be in the bookmark drag cleanup path.

On mouse down, `ClientInputHandler.onGuiMouseClicked(...)` starts drag handling:

```java
if (Minecraft.getInstance().screen == screen && input.is(keybindings.getLeftClick())) {
    handled |= this.dragRouter.startDrag(screen, input);
}
```

For bookmark overlay entries, this can create a `BookmarkDrag` through:

```text
DragRouter.startDrag(...)
BookmarkOverlay.createDragHandler(...)
BookmarkDragManager.handleDragStart(...)
BookmarkDragManager.handleClickIngredient(...)
new BookmarkDrag<>(...)
```

When the clicked bookmark is a recipe bookmark, the release/click path can open `RecipesGui`:

```text
FocusInputHandler
RecipeBookmarkElement.show(...)
RecipesGui.showRecipes(...)
RecipesGui.open()
Minecraft#setScreen(...)
```

Opening `RecipesGui` causes a GUI change, which calls:

```text
ClientInputHandler.onInitGui()
DragRouter.handleGuiChange()
DragRouter.cancelDrag()
```

The current `DragRouter.cancelDrag()` implementation cancels the registered handler list and then clears `dragStartedCallback`:

```java
public void cancelDrag() {
    for (IDragHandler handler : this.handlers) {
        handler.handleDragCanceled();
    }
    this.dragStartedCallback = null;
}
```

However, the bookmark overlay drag handler is wrapped by `ProxyDragHandler`:

```java
@Override
public void handleDragCanceled() {
    this.source.get().handleDragCanceled();
}
```

Because the screen has already changed to `RecipesGui`, `source.get()` may no longer return the same handler that originally created the `BookmarkDrag`. It can resolve to a different handler or `NullDragHandler`, so `BookmarkDragManager.stopDrag()` is not called.

At the same time, `DragRouter.cancelDrag()` clears `dragStartedCallback`, so the later release path cannot call `handleDragComplete(...)` on the original drag handler either.

This can leave `BookmarkDragManager.bookmarkDrag` alive, and `BookmarkOverlay.drawTooltips(...)` continues to draw it via:

```java
bookmarkDragManager.drawDraggedItem(guiGraphics, mouseX, mouseY)
```

which renders the ingredient at the mouse cursor.

## Suspected Cause

`DragRouter.cancelDrag()` drops the actual active drag callback without canceling it directly.

This is fragile when a drag starts under one GUI state and a GUI change occurs before mouse release, especially when the active drag handler is accessed through `ProxyDragHandler`.

## Possible Fix

Cancel the actual active drag handler before falling back to canceling all registered handlers:

```java
public void cancelDrag() {
    if (this.dragStartedCallback != null) {
        this.dragStartedCallback.handleDragCanceled();
        this.dragStartedCallback = null;
        return;
    }

    for (IDragHandler handler : this.handlers) {
        handler.handleDragCanceled();
    }
}
```

Alternatively, `ProxyDragHandler` could remember the delegate that handled `handleDragStart(...)` and forward `handleDragComplete(...)` / `handleDragCanceled()` to that same delegate instead of resolving `source.get()` again after the screen state has changed.

## Notes

This was reproduced with vanilla crafting recipe bookmarks, so it does not appear to be related to custom recipe widgets or modded recipe layouts.

issues.title: [Feature Request]: Optional client-side fallback for vanilla recipes when JEI isn't installed server-side
issues.body:
Since Minecraft 1.21.2, the vanilla server only syncs *unlocked* recipes to the
client and keeps full recipe data server-side. As a result, JEI can no longer
show recipes when it isn't installed on the server. This makes JEI's core
feature unavailable on the many survival/multiplayer servers that don't (or
can't) run JEI server-side.

I understand this is a Mojang-side change, not something JEI introduced, and that
datapack / modded / server-custom recipes genuinely can't be reconstructed on the
client. This request is only about the recipes that *are* deterministic.


An **opt-in** client-side fallback that reconstructs or bundles **vanilla**
recipes, so that at least vanilla crafting/smelting/etc. recipes stay viewable
when JEI (or a compatible recipe sync) isn't present on the server. Ideally:

- Off by default, or auto-enabled only when JEI is not detected on the server.
- Clearly labeled as a "vanilla-only fallback" so users understand that
  modded/custom recipes still require server-side JEI.


Community mods already do this and prove it's feasible:
- Client Recipe Fix (JEI/REI) — restores vanilla recipes on the client.
- Just Enough Serverless Recipes (JESR) — injects a client-side fallback recipe map.

It would be great to have this as a first-class, maintained option in JEI itself,
rather than relying on third-party mods that may lag behind JEI/MC updates.

### Additional context

Related: #4237, #4122.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Support UniversalRecipeTransferHandlers for multiple MenuTypes from the same class
issues.body:
### Suggestion

ExtendedAE declares two different `MenuType`s within the same class, and while I can handle the process of transferring the recipe with the same handler, the underlying registry prevents registering more than one handler per class. Additionally, `IUniversalRecipeTransferHandler` is defined such that a handler may only handle one `MenuType`.
Changing either the underlying registry to use `MenuType` as the primary key instead of a `class`, or refactoring `IUniversalRecipeTransferHandler` to allow handlers to support multiple `MenuType`s would be very helpful for addon developers looking to add transfer support to menus defined this way.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Support identifying administrators from permission plugins
issues.body:
### Suggestion

In server environments that use modern permission management plugins such as LuckPerms, JEI's admin features (like _enableCheatModeForOp_, _enableCheatModeForCreative_, and _enableCheatModeForGive_) will not function properly. At least it doesn't work properly on my server. Is this because JEI only checks the original ops.json file to determine if a player is an administrator, without taking into account the actual permission system used by the server?
Many servers no longer use the original OP system, instead opting for plugins like LuckPerms to achieve more granular permission control. These plugins typically do not write data to the ops.json file. 

Suggested solution:  
JEI should provide a more flexible administrator identification mechanism, such as:  
- Prioritize permission node checks: Before reading the ops.json file, first verify whether the player has specific permission nodes (e.g., _jei.admin_, _jei.cheatmode_).  
- Support generic permission plugin API: Query player permissions via Vault or by directly integrating with LuckPerms API.  
- Configurable detection sources: Add an option in the JEI configuration file that allows server administrators to choose how JEI obtains administrator status information (e.g., _opcheck = ["ops.json", "vault", "luckperms"]_).

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Treat `RecipeDisplay` as source-of-truth
issues.body:
### Suggestion

I'm not quite sure if this is a bug report or just an experience report for someone consuming the JEI API, so I'm being a little conservative here and reporting this as a suggestion.

Recent versions of Minecraft have split up the code governing how recipes should be displayed in the recipe book (`Recipe.display()`, `DisplayInfo`) from the core recipe logic (`Recipe.matches`/`Recipe.assemble`). This means that it's possible to implement custom recipes that appear as shaped recipes in the recipe book, but do not directly subclass `ShapedRecipe`.

However, JEI does not support this.
 - A recipe is only counted as shaped, if it [subclasses `ShapedRecipe`/`JeiShapedRecipe`](https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/blob/5aaca7c78e987ba663fccaa8e89bfda8537ab77b/Library/src/main/java/mezz/jei/library/plugins/vanilla/crafting/CraftingCategoryExtension.java#L15-L37), rather than whether it returns a `ShapedCraftingRecipeDisplay`.
 - [Only the first recipe in `Recipe.display()`](https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems/blob/5aaca7c78e987ba663fccaa8e89bfda8537ab77b/Library/src/main/java/mezz/jei/library/plugins/vanilla/crafting/CraftingCategoryExtension.java#L60) is shown to the user.

One place where this causes friction is when implementing a recipe resolver. as one must [construct a full `ShapedRecipe`](https://github.com/cc-tweaked/CC-Tweaked/blob/5adb1aa0d9dc81d195b0c6d2dc2eb625f1923966/projects/common/src/client/java/dan200/computercraft/client/integration/jei/RecipeResolver.java#L40-L52) (including a recipe ID and `ShapedRecipePattern`), despite most of that information going unused.

It I think it probably makes sense to change `CraftingCategoryExtension.{getWidth,getHeight}()` to use the display info, rather than hard-coding `ShapedRecipe` directly.

However, thinking more long-term/breaking change, I wonder if it makes sense to stop using `RecipeHolder<CraftingRecipe>` as the atomic definition of a recipe, and instead operate with `DisplayInfo` (or some wrapper over it) directly, much like vanilla does?

issues.body: ### Suggestion I am playing a modpack involving GregTech and KubeJS where I created a "Super Recipe" (a large multi-block machine). This recipe has a small number of inputs (e.g., 17 items) but a massive number of outputs (e.g., 200+ items and fluids). The current problem is Layout Logic: JEI seems to center the Input slots vertically relative to the total height of the Output slots. Because the Output list is extremely long (extending far beyond the screen height), the Input slots are "centered" into a position that is effectively off-screen (or buried deep down), leaving the top of the GUI blank. **I suggest two potential improvements to handle "Massive Recipes":** 1. Vertical Alignment Option (Top Alignment) Please add a configuration option or render logic to allow Top Alignment for recipe slots. Current behavior: Inputs are vertically centered relative to Outputs. Desired behavior: Inputs start rendering from the top-left available slot, regardless of how long the Output list is. This ensures inputs are always visible even if the output list is huge. 2. Pagination/Scrolling for a Single Recipe Currently, the mouse wheel changes between "Recipe A" and "Recipe B". I propose adding a mechanism to handle a Single Recipe that exceeds the GUI height: Internal Scrollbar: Add a scrollbar specifically for the ingredient grid if it overflows the RecipeGuiHeight. Or "Sub-pages": If a recipe has too many items to fit in one view, split that single recipe into multiple pages (e.g., "Page 1/3 of Recipe A") that the user can click through, rather than just clipping the items off-screen. - Describe alternatives you've considered : I tried using the mouse wheel, but it switches to the next recipe category or the next recipe ID, rather than scrolling up/down the current large recipe. I've tried changing the game interface size, but it still doesn't display fully.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Add a way to remove ingredients from the ingredients sidebar without removing them from recipes
issues.body:
### Suggestion

## Problem

Calling `removeIngredientsAtRuntime` is currently notably more aggressive than using item hiding mode to hide an ingredient, as it doesn't just remove the ingredient from the sidebar, but also removes it from recipe catalysts and from recipe ingredients and outputs. It is possible it also hides recipes that only craft hidden ingredients, but I am uncertain on this detail.

This problem is especially odd when hiding ingredient subtypes; if you have a subtype that is not included in any creative tab, you can add it to a catalyst just fine. However, if its in a creative tab and you remove it, it now cannot be added to a catalyst.

## Context

Tinkers' Construct has a lot of items with NBT variants, such as our tables, anvils, tools, and filled tanks. We have specific creative tabs with search bars for searching many of these NBT variants. However, pack makers have often expressed a desire to hide these variants from JEI. Since there is no way to tell JEI to not include an item from one of our search tabs, we currently hide them by removing ingredients at runtime, which causes the problem above.

## Workaround

The suggested workaround is to hide the items from our creative tabs instead of using remove ingredient at runtime. However, this is problematic as that renders our creative tabs mostly useless for players who wish to find those filled tanks or tool material variants.

Another workaround would be to disable our subttype interpreter, as that will cause JEI to collapse all variants in the ingredient list to 1. However, this does not give us the option to choose which variant shows, and may negatively impact the recipe view.

## Suggested Fix
### Ideal

Ideally, a way to suppress an item from showing in JEI entirely would be the way to go. This used to be possible by not putting items in the search tab, though that had other consequences such as breaking our search bar. This would double as a fix for #3882.

There might be a way to do this using `ItemDisplayParameters`, though I do not see any obvious options for how to make that happen without a modloader change. Best idea I have is some sort of wrapper on the `HolderLookup.Provider` that can be identified as JEI via class type, but that is messy.

### Simpler

A JEI method that lets us register a "creative tab item predicate" that will allow filtering creative tabs would let us remove these items at the time they would have been added to the ingredient list, again saving the need to remove them entirely (making it again double as a fix for #3882). For efficiency, this filter should be registered to a particular (set) of creative tabs, so it need not run on every creative tab from every mod.

### Simplest

The most straight forward to implement fix would be to add a variant of `removeIngredientsAtRuntime` that does not globally remove the ingredient but just removes it from the ingredient sidebar. This would allow Tinkers to continue using the approach of hiding items that are undesired per the config options but are useful in our creative tabs.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Add quick move to IGhostIngredientHandler
issues.body:
### Motivation and use case:

Being able to move ghost items from JEI to other mods is an incredibly useful feature that I tend to use often in conjunction with AE2, e.g. when setting up filters in storage busses or when partitioning my cells in the workbench. Moving many ghost items via drag & drop however is tedious and error-prone as you constantly have to move the mouse back and forth and thus always have to remember which item you already moved and which is next. It would be much quicker and easier to just shift-click ghost items into place just the way shift-clicking items moves items from player inventory to a chest for example.

I've proposed this idea 2 years ago but sadly never received any feedback (#3321) and given that 26.1 porting just started I'd like to try again to get this feature into JEI, as I'm still convinced that it will improve ease of use.

### Proposed feature:

To make things work, JEI needs to provide an additional function in IGhostIngredientHandler to let mods handle the quick move. I propose adding the following API function

```
        /**
         * Called when a quick-move (e.g. shift-click) is performed to move a ghost item.
         */
        default <I> void quickMove(T gui, ITypedIngredient<I> ingredient) {}
```

with the main design choice rationales being:
* Changing the IGhostIngredientHandler API early during the 26.1 port leaves enough time for mods that need to be ported to 26.1 anyway to adapt to this API change.
* Offering an empty default implementation lowers the bar for porting mods even further. `shouldHighlightTargets()` also offers an empty default implementation.
* The function parameters are analogous to those of `getTargetsTyped(...)` and thus should make it easy for mod authors to implement their handlers.

How to further implement this functionality on the JEI side of things is up for discussion. I'd prefer the default keybinding for the feature to be shift-click to be intuitive for people used to shift-click items into containers, e.g. chests and extend the use of that to ghost items from JEI. AE2 already offers a similar shift-click from the player inventory to ghost item slots.

It should work for the bookmarked items on the left side as well as the items on the right side. What to do with the quick-moved ingredient is up to the other mod.

### Proof-of-concept implementation:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c08fa71-84ab-4473-ae76-d8b6ca604be0

To show the viability of my approach I've hacked together a proof-of-concept implementation (https://github.com/Mithi83/JustEnoughItems/commit/2a5a9346a09888d18381b56a9007d43591e27f59) to be able to record the video for demonstration purposes. I'm not familiar with the JEI codebase and thus had to make some educated guesses and it took some debugging sessions to find out where I would be able to hook into the input handlers to intercept the shift-click. This implementation is focussed only on getting the PoC to work ignoring proper structuring of the code.

The following points are definitely not suitable for production code:
* While adding the quick move to `GhostIngredientDragManager` is convenient for rapid prototyping it probably is not where the final code should end up given the "Drag" part of the name of the class.
* Reusing `keyBindings.getTransferRecipeBookmark()` is probably not the best idea, but it already defaulted to shift-click.
* The PoC calls the API function twice, once upon mouse-down and once upon mouse-up, which is probably not what the new API should do. You can do funny things, such as quick-moving item A on mouse-down, hold the button, move to item B, release the button and quick-move item B this way as well. In my PoC the AE2 code filters out ingredients that are already in the filter and thus ignores the duplicate API calls.

### How to proceed:

I can provide a more professional implementation as a PR or you can come up with an implementation yourself if you accept this feature proposal. As for the AE2 side of things I can make a PR myself once it is in JEI, as I'm quite familiar with that codebase.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Add support for DataMaps
issues.body:
### Suggestion

Please add support for searching and displaying ingredients based on their datamap values. [Datamaps](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/1.21.1/resources/server/datamaps/) are a NeoForge feature that generalizes tags, and, like tags, can provide useful information to players. For items, the NeoForge tooltip events can be used to manually add this information. For tags, this information is automatically appended (and searchable). However, there appears to be no side-effect free way to manipulate tooltips on fluid stacks. This is a problem that only arises when a mod displays fluidstacks in a GUI, so I don't anticipate a solution from NeoForge.

Personal motivation: For one of my mods, I would like to display additional information in all contexts, including the search grid, and make this information searchable. Currently, there appears to be no way to add a tooltip (or tooltip callback) to a fluidstack that renders in all contexts. Tags are automatically supported. It would be nice if I could provide a callback that let JEI parse my Datamap, and render sensible, searchable, tooltip lines.

issues.title: [Bug]: [1.21.10 Fabric] Crash on load due to non-ASCII character in Grindstone Disenchantment Recipe ID
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

1.  Use Minecraft version `1.21.10`.
2.  Use Fabric Loader version `0.17.3` or later.
3.  Include **Just Enough Items (JEI)** version `26.1.0.16` (or later) along with the attached list of mods.
4.  Launch the game (client-side or server-side).

The crash occurs during the recipe registration phase, specifically when JEI attempts to generate/register Grindstone Disenchantment recipes. The crash is consistently reproducible on load.

### Expected Behavior

The game should load successfully, and JEI should register all recipes (including Grindstone Disenchantment recipes) without encountering any errors related to invalid characters in `ResourceLocations`.

### Actual Behavior

The game crashes immediately during the loading phase due to a `Packet handling error`. The specific error points to an invalid character (`\u0661` - Arabic-Indic digit '1') in the `ResourceLocation` of a Grindstone disenchantment recipe, as seen in the stack trace originating from `mezz.jei.library.plugins.vanilla.grindstone.GrindstoneRecipeMaker`.

**Error Location:**
`net.minecraft.class_151: Non [a-z0-9/._-] character in path of location: minecraft:grindstone.disenchantment.item.minecraft.wooden_shovel.efficiency.\u0661`

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

Minecraft: `1.21.10` Mod Loader: `Fabric - 26.1.0.16`

### Extra Notes (Optional)

The crash is caused by an invalid character (the Arabic-Indic digit **`\u0661`** which represents the number **"1"**) being used in a `ResourceLocation` path for a Grindstone disenchantment recipe.

The invalid ID is:
`minecraft:grindstone.disenchantment.item.minecraft.wooden_shovel.efficiency.\u0661`

This error occurs deep within the JEI codebase (`mezz.jei.library.plugins.vanilla.grindstone.GrindstoneRecipeMaker`), suggesting that either:

1.  JEI is incorrectly generating a recipe ID containing this character.
2.  Or, another installed mod is introducing an enchantment/item level (`Efficiency \u0661`) that causes JEI's recipe generation logic to fail.

I have already attempted switching the game language to English, but the issue persists, indicating the character is hardcoded or generated, not user-inputted.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Add Configuration for toggle on/off server-sync mode
issues.body:
### Suggestion

If possible, add a feature where we can enable/disable server-sync mode, so that when we join a server (that doesn’t have the JEI mod on the server) and server-sync mode is disabled, the recipes come only from the client data. (Similar to JEI versions 1.21.1 and below, but with the option to turn it on or off). This way, it can be adjusted according to needs. There are cases where players can’t see recipes on public servers that don’t have the JEI mod. 

### Additional Suggestion

Also add a "Save Recipe" feature. So we first enter the Singleplayer world, then go to the inventory, to the JEI UI section, there is "Save Recipe." This feature allows you to save recipes to use when we join a server even if that server doesn’t have the JEI mod. It's similar to the bookmark feature, but the difference is that this is saved globally and stores recipes for all items.

### Consequences

I understand the consequences of using recipes from the client data, as they are not 100% the same as the server’s recipes (especially on servers with plugins; on vanilla, the recipes are usually 100% the same). But this feature can be enabled or disabled depending on the player’s needs.

issues.title: [Suggestion]: Add Filter to Uses/Recipes (especially 1.12)
issues.body:
### Suggestion

Problem:
Many items have oredict tags like `dye`, `anyLog`, etc. When trying to find what items can be made with an item, these tags often are the majority of recipes. This makes it hard to find recipes that certain items are REQUIRED for

Solution:
One of
1. Add a filter bar to filter down uses. Not sure what the best workflow would be but maybe something:
ex.
a. Get uses of "Red Flower Petal" from Botania
b. All uses pop up as normal
c. Fill new search bar at the bottom of the UI with `-$dyeRed @Botania`
d. Only the recipes that can't be replaced with `$dyeRed` and are in Botania would be shown

ex. 
a. Get recipes of "Iron Ingot"
b. All recipes pop up as normal
c. Fill new search bar at the bottom at the bottom of the UI with `-iron_block`
d. Only the recipes that don't use `iron_block` in them would be shown


2. Let searching of uses/recipes in the JEI search bar
ex.
Searching `<"red flower petal" -$dyeRed @Botania"`would show all the items that would show up in 1d (ie. Botania items that can be made with "red flower petals", but NOT other $dyeRed items

ex.
Searching  `>"iron ingot" -iron_block` would show all the items that can make iron ingots that don't have `iron_block` in the name


Request that this is added to 1.12.2 first please (many modpacks still use it)

issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

Install Minecraft 1.21.1 with NeoForge 21.1.193.

Install ToolBelt 2.2.6 and JEI 19.22.0.315.

Launch Minecraft and attempt to load into a world.

Result: The game crashes immediately due to a keybind-related NullPointerException from ToolBelt.

ToolBelt mod keybinds should register and function correctly, irrespective of the JEI version.

With JEI 19.22.0.315, ToolBelt’s keybind (OPEN_BELT_SLOT_KEYBIND) fails to register and results in a crash with the following exception:
 {java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "net.minecraft.client.KeyMapping.consumeClick()" because "dev.gigaherz.toolbelt.client.ClientEvents.OPEN_BELT_SLOT_KEYBIND" is null} at toolbelt@2.2.6/dev.gigaherz.toolbelt.client.ClientEvents.handleKeys(ClientEvents.java:88)

Downgrading JEI to 19.21.0.247 resolves the crash entirely, indicating a specific conflict introduced in JEI 19.22.0.315.
